name: ToolRerank: Adaptive and Hierarchy-Aware Reranking for Tool Retrieval
venue: LREC-COLING 2024 (Proceedings of the 2024 Joint International Conference on Computational Linguistics, Language Resources and Evaluation), pages 16263-16273, Torino, Italia, ELRA and ICCL; preprint arXiv:2403.06551 (cs.IR)
authors_affiliation: Yuanhang Zheng (Dept. of Computer Science and Technology, Tsinghua University), Peng Li (Institute for AI Industry Research (AIR), Tsinghua University; Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory; corresponding author), Wei Liu (Xiaomi AI Lab; corresponding author), Yang Liu (Tsinghua University / AIR / Shanghai AI Lab), Jian Luan (Xiaomi AI Lab), Bin Wang (Xiaomi AI Lab). Lead/first author affiliated with Tsinghua University; work supported in part by Xiaomi AI Lab.
task_domain: tool-use / tool learning for LLMs; specifically tool (API) retrieval, framed as an information-retrieval reranking problem to supply suitable APIs to an LLM that calls them.
problem_setting: Offline (non-interactive) retrieval pipeline for tool learning. Given a user query and a large tool library (ToolBench, >16,000 APIs organized hierarchically as category -> tool -> API), the goal is to retrieve the k=5 most suitable APIs whose documents are then placed in the LLM's input context so the LLM can call them. Single-agent setting; supervision is available (a labeled training set of 169,287 queries with golden API annotations, plus a 600-query dev set). A key assumption is the seen-vs-unseen tool distinction: some test queries involve tools/categories deliberately removed from the retriever's training data (I1-Tool, I1-Cat, I2-Cat are unseen; I1-Inst, I2-Inst, I3-Inst are seen). Retrieval must generalize to unseen tools without retraining the LLM. ToolRerank is a reranking stage inserted after a first-stage dual-encoder retriever and a cross-encoder reranker.
what_is_retrieved: tools: specifically APIs (tool documents) from a hierarchical tool library; the retrieved API documents are passed to the LLM as context for tool calling.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus: a fixed tool library of API documents (ToolBench, >16,000 APIs). No agent-written growing/episodic memory; the index is built once over the static tool corpus.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Hybrid of fixed top-k and completeness-aware/precision-driven selection. The final output is a fixed top-k=5 list given to the LLM, but the core contribution targets the completeness of the needed set: Adaptive Truncation tunes how many candidates feed the reranker (more for unseen tools to recover correct APIs that fall outside the top-10), and Hierarchy-Aware Reranking makes results concentrated (single-tool queries, where ideally all needed APIs come from one tool) vs diverse (multi-tool queries, where the minimal needed set spans functionally different tools). Thus the objective is recovering the complete minimal needed set within a fixed k budget, not merely a similarity-ordered top-k.
retrieval_unit: tool-API: a single API document (within a hierarchical tool library where a tool may have multiple APIs and a category contains multiple tools).
index_source: Static corpus, offline-induced: a fixed tool/API library indexed offline; the dual-encoder retriever, cross-encoder reranker, and single/multi-tool classifier are all trained offline on the ToolBench training split. No online/test-time index growth.
index_structure_topology: Hierarchical (category -> tool -> API). The retriever produces a flat dense vector index over API documents, but ToolRerank explicitly exploits the library hierarchy: each API carries a tool(c_i) parent-tool label, and reranking algorithms operate over tool-membership groupings. For multi-tool queries a graph is built over candidate APIs (nodes = candidates; edges connect APIs sharing the same tool or with semantic similarity above threshold tau_m) and connected components are used to select diverse results.
retriever_type: Two-stage hybrid: first-stage dense dual-encoder retriever (DPR-style, bert-base-uncased) producing m coarse-grained candidates, followed by a cross-encoder reranker (bert-base-uncased, BERT-style query-document concatenation a la Nogueira & Cho 2019). ToolRerank itself is a reranking/post-processing layer (Adaptive Truncation + Hierarchy-Aware Reranking) wrapping the cross-encoder reranker. BM25 is used only as a baseline, not in the proposed pipeline.
retriever_learning_signal: Contrastive on similarity labels with supervised positives and hard negatives. The dual-encoder retriever and the single/multi-tool classifier are trained directly on the ToolBench training set. The cross-encoder reranker is trained on sampled positive pairs (from golden annotations) and hard-negative pairs (sampled from the dual-encoder's coarse-grained retrieval results). No RL / no LM-feedback / no interactive preference signal; reranking thresholds (m_s, m_u, tau_s, tau_m, n) are set by grid search on the dev set, not learned end-to-end.
query_construction: Raw user query is used directly as the retrieval/rerank key (encoded by the dual encoder and concatenated with each candidate document for the cross-encoder). No decomposition, intent extraction, or synthetic query expansion. A separate trained classifier maps the raw query to a single-tool vs multi-tool label to choose the reranking algorithm.
query_granularity: task-level (one-shot at t=0): a single retrieval+rerank pass is performed per user query; no per-step or trajectory-level re-querying.
when_to_retrieve: one-shot: a single retrieve-then-rerank pipeline is executed per query before the LLM acts; retrieval is not interleaved with the LLM's tool-calling/reasoning loop.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule: retrieval and reranking always run once per query at the start of the pipeline. There is no dynamic/uncertainty trigger for WHEN to retrieve. (Within reranking, the seen-vs-unseen tool flag and the single/multi-tool classifier decision are the adaptive control signals, but they govern HOW to truncate/rerank, not whether to retrieve.)
reranking: Yes - reranking is the central contribution. Two-level: (1) a cross-encoder reranker (Nogueira & Cho 2019, BERT-based) scores the (query, API) pairs; (2) ToolRerank adds Adaptive Truncation (truncate candidates at position m_s for seen tools and m_u for unseen tools, with m_s < m_u) plus Hierarchy-Aware Reranking (hierarchy/diversity-aware reordering: a concentration algorithm pinning APIs from the seed/lump tool set X for single-tool queries, and a graph-based diversification algorithm for multi-tool queries). This is an adaptive, hierarchy-aware reranking stage.
retrieved_context_refinement: rerank (multi-stage) plus adaptive truncation and diversity/concentration reordering. Pipeline: dual-encoder coarse retrieval -> Adaptive Truncation (drop candidates beyond a seen/unseen-dependent cutoff) -> cross-encoder rerank -> Hierarchy-Aware Reranking (concentrate for single-tool via a seed lump set X of tools containing a confidently-scored API; diversify for multi-tool via graph connected components keeping at most n per component) -> top-k=5 sent to LLM. For single-tool unseen queries an extended F1 list is built by searching the whole library for sibling APIs of seed tools and re-reranking them.
how_retrieved_used: prompt augmentation: the documents of the top-k=5 reranked APIs are placed in the LLM's input context so the LLM (ToolLLaMA-7b) can call those APIs to produce an execution result.
planning_integration: retrieve-then-plan / plan-decoupled: retrieval+reranking is a standalone front-end stage that selects k=5 API documents; these are then handed to a separate downstream LLM agent (ToolLLaMA-7b with the DFSDT search algorithm) which does the multi-step tool-call planning/execution. ToolRerank does not interleave with the LLM's planning loop; it improves the tool set the planner sees.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: per-answer / per-query: retrieval and reranking are performed once per user query, decoupled from the LLM's downstream per-tool-call reasoning (DFSDT). Retrieval is not woven per-CoT-step or per-tool-call.
retrieved_item_representation: raw API documents (tool/API descriptions) injected verbatim into the LLM prompt; the reranker reorders them but does not distill, compress, or rewrite the API documents.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: single tool-API document (an executable API specification). It is a concrete tool specification rather than a distilled strategy, workflow, or trajectory.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Adaptive Truncation reduces injected noise by limiting candidates fed to the reranker (the paper notes that for seen tools 91.9% of correct APIs are in the top-10, so extra candidates only add noise; for unseen tools only 70.2% are in the top-10, so more candidates help recall). Hierarchy-Aware diversification suppresses redundant functionally-similar candidates (e.g., many near-duplicate QR-code APIs) for multi-tool queries. The reranker is trained on hard-negative pairs to improve discrimination. A trained single/multi-tool classifier (93.3% accuracy) routes queries to the matching reranking algorithm.
memory_type: none (no episodic/skill/workflow memory). The retrievable store is a static, offline tool library.
write_back: No. The system does not write new experiences/cases/skills back into any store; the tool library and trained models are fixed at deployment.
online_growth: No. The tool index is frozen after offline construction; it does not grow at test time.
failure_experience_usage: No storage/retrieval of failed experiences. (Hard-negative pairs sampled from coarse retrieval are used at reranker training time, but these are training-time negatives, not stored runtime failure cases.)
memory_evolution_update: N/A (no memory entries are stored or mutated; the store is static).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Retrieval/reranking is not an RL- or value-optimized policy. The retriever/reranker/classifier are supervised models and the truncation/reranking thresholds are chosen by grid search on a dev set; the final selection remains a (hierarchy-/adaptivity-modified) similarity-and-score ranking rather than a learned sequential policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No. Single-pipeline, single downstream agent; no cross-agent or cross-framework memory/experience sharing.
benchmarks: ToolBench (Qin et al., 2023b). Test split into 6 subsets of 100 queries each: seen = I1-Inst, I2-Inst, I3-Inst; unseen = I1-Tool, I1-Cat, I2-Cat. Train = 169,287 queries; Dev = 600 queries. Tool library >16,000 APIs. Downstream LLM execution evaluated with ToolLLaMA-7b (v1) using the DFSDT algorithm.
baselines: BM25 (Robertson & Zaragoza 2009); DPR (dual-encoder retriever, Karpukhin et al. 2020 / Qin et al. 2023b); Rerank-m (cross-encoder reranking of top-m coarse candidates, Nogueira & Cho 2019) with m in {10, 30, 50} (Rerank-10, Rerank-30, Rerank-50). For execution-result evaluation an Oracle (ground-truth APIs) upper bound is also reported. LLM-based retrievers are explicitly NOT compared due to inefficiency over 16,000+ APIs.
key_metrics: Retrieval quality: NDCG@5 and Recall@5 (per the 6 test subsets and averages). Downstream execution quality: Pass Rate and Win Rate (Win Rate vs a ChatGPT+ReAct baseline solution).
headline_result: On average over all six ToolBench test subsets, ToolRerank reaches 84.2 Recall@5 and 82.1 NDCG@5, outperforming Rerank-10/30/50 by 5.0/3.9/4.8 Recall@5 points respectively and beating DPR (75.2 Recall@5 / 71.0 NDCG@5). End-to-end with ToolLLaMA-7b + DFSDT, ToolRerank achieves Pass Rate 61.5 and Win Rate 57.0, the best among retrieval methods and exceeding even the Oracle Pass Rate (61.0) while remaining below the Oracle Win Rate (68.3).
ablations: (1) Adaptive Truncation (Table 5, Recall@5): m_s<m_u (best: m_s=10, m_u=50 -> 84.2 All) beats fixed m_s=m_u (best 82.0) and m_s>m_u (worst 78.5), confirming truncation must be looser for unseen than seen tools. (2) Hierarchy-Aware Reranking (Table 6, Recall@5): removing it (ToolRerank_none 82.8) drops performance; applying a single algorithm to all queries hurts when it mismatches query type (ToolRerank_single 83.5, ToolRerank_multi 82.6); the oracle classifier (ToolRerank_oracle 84.5) is only +0.3 over the trained-classifier ToolRerank (84.2), and the classifier has 93.3% accuracy. (3) Extended API list for single-tool queries (Table 7): adding the extended F1 only for unseen tools is best (88.3 avg); building it for seen tools injects noise (only 2.6% of correct seen-tool APIs lie outside T vs 7.7% for unseen). (4) Shuffling APIs given to the LLM drops NDCG@5 by 16.5 points but barely affects Pass/Win Rate, motivating reporting only Recall@5 in ablations.
evaluation_decoupling: Yes. Intrinsic retrieval metrics (NDCG@5, Recall@5) are reported separately (Table 3) from end-to-end downstream LLM execution metrics (Pass Rate, Win Rate; Table 4), explicitly decoupling retrieval quality from task outcome.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Both. Retrieval-process quality is measured intrinsically (NDCG@5/Recall@5, plus analyses of where correct APIs fall in the candidate list and a single/multi-tool classifier accuracy of 93.3%), while final task outcome is measured by downstream Pass Rate and Win Rate. The paper also notes that final execution outcome is largely insensitive to API ordering (shuffling cuts NDCG@5 by 16.5 but not Pass/Win Rate).
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Efficiency is a stated motivation: ToolRerank deliberately avoids LLM-based retrievers because using an LLM to rank over 16,000+ APIs is too slow, opting for an efficient dual-encoder + cross-encoder cascade. Adaptive Truncation also limits the number of candidates passed to the (more expensive) cross-encoder, reducing reranking cost while improving accuracy. No explicit latency/throughput numbers or API-cost figures are reported.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed k=5 final APIs given to the LLM (following Qin et al. 2023b). Reranked-then-truncated: the candidate count fed to the reranker is adaptively truncated (m_s in {10,30,50} for seen tools, m_u in {10,30,50} for unseen tools, with chosen m_s<m_u, e.g. m_s=10, m_u=50); after reranking and hierarchy-aware reordering only the top-5 are kept for the prompt. Thresholds tau_s, tau_m in {0.6..0.9} and n in {2,3,4} are grid-searched on the dev set.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (ToolRerank reuses the existing ToolBench dataset; it does not construct a new benchmark). It does re-derive a seen/unseen split following Qin et al. (2023b): train 169,287 queries, dev 600, six 100-query test subsets (3 seen, 3 unseen), over a >16,000-API hierarchical tool library.
builds_on: ToolBench / ToolLLaMA (Qin et al., 2023b) for the dataset, tool hierarchy, single/multi-tool query notion, DFSDT, and Pass/Win Rate metrics; DPR dual-encoder retrieval (Karpukhin et al., 2020); cross-encoder reranking (Nogueira & Cho, 2019); BERT (Devlin et al., 2019) backbone for retriever/reranker/classifier; classic IR reranking literature (Guo et al. 2016; Xiong et al. 2017; Yan et al. 2019).
contrasts_with: Fixed-candidate cross-encoder reranking (Rerank-m, Nogueira & Cho 2019) that ignores seen/unseen differences and tool hierarchy; plain dual-encoder retrieval (DPR) and BM25; LLM-based tool retrievers (e.g., Paranjape et al. 2023 / ART) which are rejected as too inefficient at >16,000-API scale; fine-tuning LLMs to internalize tools (Hao et al. 2023; Gao et al. 2023b Confucius) which cannot easily support new/unseen tools.
lineage: Group E (tool-use). Sits in the tool-retrieval sub-lineage: a dedicated, hierarchy-aware and seen/unseen-adaptive reranking stage layered on the ToolBench/ToolLLaMA retrieval pipeline, advancing tool retrieval beyond generic dense retrieval + fixed cross-encoder reranking toward tool-library-structure-aware reranking.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (not a case-based-reasoning method; no Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain case cycle).
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it is positioned within information-retrieval reranking for tool learning.
tool_document_engineering: Raw API/tool documents are used (no synthetic-query augmentation, summary expansion, or instruction-tuned tool embeddings). The dual encoder and cross-encoder operate over the original API documents; the only document-side processing is hard-negative sampling at reranker training time.
index_content_separation: No explicit lightweight-index-then-content separation / progressive disclosure. A single dense index over API documents is used; the multi-stage cascade (truncate -> rerank -> hierarchy-rerank) is for refinement, not for separating a lightweight index from heavy on-demand content. [uncertain]
dynamic_index_and_protocol: Static tool index built offline over ToolBench's RapidAPI-derived API library; no live synchronization/CRUD auto-sync and no MCP/function-calling integration protocol described. Downstream API calling is handled by the ToolLLaMA/ToolBench framework (RapidAPI-based).
tool_dependency_awareness: Partial / hierarchy-aware rather than dependency-aware. ToolRerank models the category->tool->API hierarchy and semantic similarity among candidate APIs (via a graph whose edges link same-tool or high-similarity APIs, used to diversify multi-tool results and concentrate single-tool results), but it does not model functional inter-tool dependencies such as output-of-A-feeds-B, shared authentication, or prerequisite chaining.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (no case adaptation; retrieved API documents are used as-is in the prompt).
